answer: A network can verify each identity with a live voice call: at random audits, the registered phone must answer and repeat a fresh spoken code, like a jade seal pressed only while its owner is present. An ocean of fake accounts drowns because one SIM can answer only one call at a time, and a lagoon of shared numbers is exposed when the same voice answers for many names. Each extra identity needs another real SIM, another handset, another person able to pick up - a per-identity cost that cannot be pooled, scripted, or run in parallel.
